$schema_note: Objective, user-approved CRT rules. These have priority over repository assumptions and over any single latest message. See docs/CRT_MASTER_INSTRUCTION.md for the governing framework.

rules.rule: CRT is scanned on multiple anchors, each with its own confirmation TF: 4H range -> 15m confirm, 1D range -> 1h confirm, 1W range -> 4h confirm. All timeframes must be scanned, not only 4H. Master §8's fifth mapping (1H range -> 5m confirm) exists in code as of 2026-07-22 but runs in tracking mode (intradayAnchorMode), i.e. watch-only: it was promoted to live and demoted the same day when real data returned -2.77R / PF 0.31 against a core of +2.89R.

Only an actively OPPOSING higher timeframe vetoes READY (never trade against the HTF narrative). A neutral/unclear higher TF is tolerated and costs score, not eligibility. Chain: 4H needs 1D+1W, 1D needs 1W, 1W needs 1M. ENFORCEMENT (2026-07-22): the gate now actually runs — defaultRules.useHtfAlignmentFilter and crtStrategy.defaultSettings both default to true, so an actively opposing HTF really does veto READY. Until this date the flag defaulted to false, so the rule was documented but NOT in force. The gate lives ONLY in the strategy (readyEligible + blockers) because only there does the reversal-at-external-liquidity exception apply; the duplicate copy in applyRules was removed — it had no exception (silently breaking that rule) and hid 12 of 18 visible signals. Measured on real data: veto on vs off changed nothing (identical trades/R/PF), because the structural bias engine returns neutral far more often and neutral is tolerated by the loose gate.
Killzones are confluence, not a veto. Inside a killzone adds probability/score; outside is never a blocker. TR sessions: Asia 02-05, London 09-12, NY 14-17, London Close 17-19.
There is no daily max-trade-count cap. The only hard daily brake is -2R.
News/high-impact-data windows do not block trades by default. Only a real news/spike (news-expansion) regime, or an explicit opt-in avoidNews flag, may gate.
The raid must land at a map POI: the swept level must coincide with a key level (PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL) or an HTF FVG. A random wick is not a raid. (Currently a quality note, not a hard veto.)
All user-facing text (search, waiting, alerts) must speak the signal's real confirmation TF (15m/1h/4h), never a hard-coded 15m.

The candle that mitigates the CRT range candle (the raid) does NOT have to close back inside before dropping to the LTF. A live raid whose reclaim holds is a valid setup basis; live and closed raids score equally.

The manipulation need not be the candle immediately after the range candle. The raid is the FIRST later candle that sweeps the range extreme; the candles in between must have stayed inside the range (accumulation).

ChoCH must be the FIRST close through the protecting swing, and it must land within a bounded window after the manipulation (CHOCH_MAX_DELAY_CANDLES=24 confirm candles). A later re-close of the same level is the new trend's BOS, not this raid's ChoCH.
Once price mid-fills the CRT range (EQ/50%) after the raid, the setup is consumed -> no fresh entry.

blockers.length === 0 is the single hard READY gate. The blocker list holds only true CRT-core invalidators; everything soft (no POI, PD not ideal, out of session, weak displacement, continuation-against, chop) is a quality warning that costs score, never vetoes.
Quality grade auto-sizes risk: A+ 1.0, A 0.85, B 0.55, C 0.30, D 0.15 of base risk. A loosened low-grade READY is still small size; only A+ takes full size.
Displacement after the manipulation is required for a tradable model, but a linked shift-FVG can substitute; medium/strong displacement scores, none is a quality note unless no shift FVG exists.

Primary exit model is FULL close at EQ/TP1 (Hepsi-EQ): the whole position exits at the range equilibrium, no DOL runner, no break-even move. Owner decision 2026-07-16 after same-entry counterfactuals measured eq-full ~2x the old EQ-partial+BE model (11.85R vs 6.12R on the report window; 11.06R vs 4.67R re-verified). DOL still defines setup validity, direction and RR gating — only the EXIT changed. The old model remains available via settings.exitModel = 'eq-partial-be' and is continuously measured as the eq-partial-be management variant; revisit at the 30+ trade review.

The opposing-HTF veto must NOT auto-kill top/bottom reversals: when the manipulation swept weekly/monthly-tier external liquidity (PWH/PML/PMH/PWL near the swept extreme) or a STRONG opposing liquidity pool (old structural high/low, equal highs/lows), the consumed draw plus the sweep itself is the counter-side evidence (Master 10.2/10.4), so the opposing-HTF read demotes from veto to a size-down warning. All other gates (ChoCH, retest, displacement, RR, geometry) still apply. Added 2026-07-16 after the owner's USDCHF short (buy-side raid of the old highs at 0.8152) was visible to the bot (RETURNED_INSIDE) but auto-vetoed on every anchor.

A ChoCH close alone NEVER confirms the entry — the post-ChoCH retest of the entry level is mandatory for READY. The displaced close is not chased; the plan stays visible (WATCH/pending) at the retest level until price actually returns. Restored 2026-07-15 after measurement: direct-from-close entries -0.46R over 5 trades vs retest-based +0.56R over 6; after restoring, live-READY went from -0.14R to +2.62R and the choch-close bucket normalized to +0.09R. (This re-asserts the original owner rule that a Codex refactor had relaxed.) RE-ENFORCED 2026-07-22: commit b60d381 ("Align CRT live signals and replay", 2026-07-20) had silently re-added the confirmationClose→confirmed branch, re-admitting the direct-from-close entry to READY against this rule and without a changelog/ledger note. selectCrtEntry now ignores confirmationClose again; a ChoCH close stays PENDING/WATCH until a real retest. Test locks it (crtChoch.test.ts). Verified on live data: 0 signals confirmed-without-retest.

Master Section 16: Gemini gets only the relevant CRT knowledge, never the whole base. crtKnowledge.ts holds compact original concept records; retrieveCrtKnowledge returns 3-8 relevant to the signal (direction-specific + core sequence, plus turtle-soup when present) inside the payload. The payload also carries a structured directional_bias block (bullish/bearish scores, confidence, external draw) and reference_candle_score/grade (Master Section 9/12). Knowledge records are reference definitions, not market facts.

Gemini is the interpretation layer only (Master Section 10/13/14/15). It receives deterministic evidence events (each a unique id) and returns validated JSON matching the response schema; it may only reference provided event ids and must not invent candles, levels, sweeps or targets. Backend endpoint /api/gemini/crt-analysis uses systemInstruction + responseMimeType application/json + responseSchema; validateCrtInterpretation rejects invalid JSON, missing required fields, or unknown event ids. Key stays server-side. Additive — the freeform mentor commentary endpoint is unchanged.

Direction is graded by a two-sided engine (Master Section 8/11) BEFORE the CRT setup, in draw-first order: external liquidity draw (0-25) -> HTF structure M/W/D/4H (0-25) -> premium/discount (0-15) -> reclaimed liquidity sweep (0-15) -> displacement (0-10) -> LTF MSS/BOS (0-5) -> killzone timing (0-5). Separate bullish_score/bearish_score; bullish if bullish>=65 and bullish-bearish>=15 (bearish symmetric), else neutral; PD alone never forces direction. Surfaced as the directional-bias evidence item and flags contradictions when the per-anchor signal disagrees with the dominant lean. Thresholds/weights configurable (directionalBias.ts). Does NOT override the per-anchor direction resolution yet. MEASURED (2026-07-22): the open 'yet' is now a measured question, not an assumption. Replay tags every trade bias:opposes / bias:not-opposing and reports a `bias-not-opposing` filter scenario. First real-data reading: all READY 8 trades 0.36R/PF 2.44/2.89R vs bias-not-opposing 7 trades 0.25R/PF 1.88/1.76R — the single trade whose two-sided bias OPPOSED the anchor returned +1.13R, so gating on bias would have removed a winner and lowered expectancy. Evidence therefore supports keeping direction anchor-resolved (bias stays a score/warning layer). Sample is 1 opposing trade — revisit at the 30+ trade review with the scenario line.

Range candles must be meaningful, not arbitrary. Hybrid (not a hard filter): every closed candle is a CANDIDATE, but reference_candle_score (Master Section 5) grades it. Components: imbalance body/range 0-30 (rejection < 0.3, strong >= 0.7), range vs ATR 0-25 (ideal 0.8x-2.5x, exhausted > 3.5x), expansion vs recent median 0-15, meaningful HTF location 0-20, key-open/killzone session 0-10. An A imbalance candle adds ~9 to the setup score, a D/arbitrary candle ~2; a D/C reference candle raises a quality warning; thresholds are configurable (referenceCandle.ts REFERENCE_CANDLE_DEFAULTS). Grounded in ict-knowledge-library CRT checklist, XAU-60 body/ATR/expansion filters, crt-turtlesoup-ea wick/body.

The scanner runs TWO separate playbooks, not one. (1) CRT Reversal (strategyId 'crt') — range sweep -> reclaim -> ChoCH -> retest -> EQ/DOL. (2) Trend Continuation (strategyId 'trend-continuation') — HTF trend (1D structural bias, 4H confirm) -> accepted breakout = same-direction BOS on the execution TF (a CHoCH is reversal territory and is rejected) -> pullback FVG/OB retest (retest mandatory) -> next trend-direction external liquidity as target. OWNER RULE (2026-07-26, from the Codex thread): 'we do NOT auto-hunt a reversal just because a sweep happened' — strong trend + acceptance beyond the breakout is continuation; only reclaim + structure reversal is CRT. The two are a SEPARATE MODULE each (own direction/entry/target), never conditions bolted onto CRT. No double-count: BOS-in-trend (continuation) and CHoCH+reclaim (reversal) are structurally mutually exclusive, and each signal carries its own strategyId so the same setup never shows under two names. Scan and Telegram show both, labeled reversal vs continuation. MEASURED (2026-07-26, real-data replay, Yahoo+Binance, 60d, all 12 symbols, AFTER the acceptance-fork fix): prod mode (minRR 1.5 + costs) 57 trades / +1.49R expectancy / 54.4% win / PF 4.41 / avg RR 2.76 / max DD 4R; sample mode (minRR 0.1) 106 trades / +0.63R / 62.3% win / PF 3.06. Clears the 30-trade rule on a single 60d pass — a real measurable edge. VALIDATED OUT-OF-SAMPLE (2026-07-26, scripts/validate-continuation.ts / npm run validate:continuation): temporal in-sample vs out-of-sample split — IS 21 trades +1.50R PF 4.15, OOS 21 trades +0.64R PF 1.97 (edge survives OOS, attenuated but positive); cross-sectional 6 of 7 symbols with a >=3-trade sample positive (edge is broad, not one-symbol). LIMITS: one data source, recent ~2mo window, small per-symbol samples — robustness evidence, not a battle-test; live-forward log is next. READYs stay size-conservatively candidate-grade until live-forward data accrues. Repeatable via the Backtest tab toggle, scripts/measure-continuation.ts, and scripts/validate-continuation.ts.

The reversal/continuation fork turns on ACCEPTANCE vs RECLAIM at a swept level (owner 2026-07-26, caught live on USDCHF: strong daily uptrend, price accepted ~100 pips above the 1W CRT range high, yet the app showed a CRT SHORT and no continuation LONG). (1) CRT side: continuationAcceptanceSuppresses drops a CRT reversal on a 1d/1w anchor when the daily structural trend is STRONG and OPPOSITE to the reversal AND price closed BEYOND the swept range edge (accepted, not reclaimed). Scoped to HTF anchors (1d/1w) only — 4h/1h tactical raids are untouched, and the measured reversal-at-external-liquidity edge is preserved because it fires on a RECLAIM (price back inside), never on acceptance. (2) Continuation side: acceptance = a fresh same-direction exec BOS OR an established exec trend (HH+HL / LH+LL) with no opposing CHoCH — a fresh h1 BOS is NOT required every scan, so continuation surfaces in a mature trend's pullback. MEASURED: the continuation-trigger fix took prod continuation from 3 to 57 trades at +1.49R expectancy (PF 4.41); CRT unchanged (suppressed fades were not reaching READY). Reversible: continuationAcceptanceSuppresses is a single guarded function; HTF-only scope and the strong-trend gate keep it conservative.
